title: Recognition: A Manual
claim: Recognition is not an experience to be produced but a fact to be noticed: this manual gives the shortest rigorous path from the ordinary sense of being a separate person to the recognition of oneself as the whole, with the texts’ own practices and tests.

purpose.impact: A single sitting that moves the reader from ‘I am a separate person’ to ‘I am the whole’, with nothing to believe and nothing to join.
purpose.reader: The sceptical, intelligent reader who will not join anything but cannot stop asking whether experience proves what it seems to.
purpose.realisation: Recognition is not a state to be acquired later; it is the fact already the case, and the reader can test it on the page before finishing the book.
non_goals: no devotional tone and no promises of special states
no invented practice — every method is the text’s own

pages.note: 36 entries as spreads (72pp) + front 10 + glossary 8 + index 6 + end 4 = 100, padded to 108.

sections_plan.purpose: why the ordinary self feels incomplete; what misidentification costs
what is always already present in experience
you are not the body, the mind, or the thought
the world is not outside awareness, without solipsism
desire, knowing, action — icchā, jñāna, kriyā
the actual practices, placed from the texts
how you know it is working
post-recognition life: nothing special, everything changed

inclusion: every entry faces its explanation: brief (C1 essence), what (sense), how (the text's own practice), sign (the text's own claimed effect) — feel optional
content is extract-and-place from named sources and layers; clarity-edits only after placing; no source = block stays off the page (fail closed)
whole book must preflight under the template page ceiling with the template style before the build stage opens
each entry carries four placed blocks: Cost, Recognition, Practice, Sign
sources are Spanda, Tantrasāra and the VBT verses not consumed by the exhaustive references
exclusion: no entry may appear in another book — one prayer, one book (cross-book id and IAST uniqueness is gate-enforced)
no agent-written prose anywhere in the entry fields; translations are ours, Lakshmanjoo/Dyczkowski prose is never printed beyond brief attributed quotation
no PDF build before content, structure, and formatting are confirmed — the build stage is the LAST stage of the pipeline, never the first
no verse already assigned to a reference volume in this series
no invented practice and no agent-written prose
